title_en: Song Lili v. Suqian City Construction Bureau — dispute over ruling on housing demolition compensation and resettlement
keywords_en: administrative; ruling on compensation and resettlement for house demolition; first instance; basic people's court; Jiangsu Province; natural person; legal person; Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition; Jiangsu Province Regulations on the Administration of Urban House Demolition; validity of appraisal report; administrative adjudication procedure; clarity of property rights exchange content; partial support; house demolition; compensation and resettlement ruling; unilaterally commissioned appraisal; administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Song Lili v. Suqian Construction Bureau — dispute over housing demolition compensation and resettlement ruling

[Ruling Summary]

Where an administrative authority, when making a ruling on a dispute over compensation for housing demolition, violates the provisions of regulations by relying on an appraisal report commissioned unilaterally by the demolition party, and the person whose property is being demolished raises an objection, it shall be determined that the administrative ruling lacks sufficient main evidence.

Plaintiff: Song Lili, female, manager of Suqian Catering Service Company, Jiangsu Province, residing at Xingfu Middle Road, Suqian, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Suqian Construction Bureau, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Hua Zhiming, Director of the Bureau.

Third Party: Suqian Wanxing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Jian Xinxian, Chairman of the Company.

On June 5, 2003, the Suqian Construction Bureau issued Su Jian Cai Zi [2003] No. 26 ruling on disputes over housing demolition, the main contents of which were: (1) The person whose property was being demolished, Song Lili, shall complete the demolition within 15 days from the effective date of the ruling; (2) The housing resettlement compensation (including housing compensation, moving expenses, ancillary facilities and decoration costs, temporary resettlement subsidies, and business cessation losses) shall total RMB 685,651.88; (3) After the completion of the Zhongmao Department Store project, Wanxing Company shall provide one unit of housing within that project (with an area roughly equivalent to the demolished house), and the price of the replacement house shall be determined based on the market appraisal value; (4) Wanxing Company shall arrange a transitional house for the person being demolished to reside in temporarily. Song Lili was dissatisfied with this ruling and initiated administrative litigation, filing a lawsuit with the Sucheng District People's Court of Suqian, Jiangsu Province on September 4, 2003, requesting the annulment of the ruling.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant's use of the appraisal by Fangyuan Real Estate Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fangyuan Company) as the basis for the compensation amount for the demolished house was erroneous. When the demolition party commissioned Fangyuan Company to conduct the appraisal, it violated the principles of fairness, justice, and openness. By directly using this appraisal report as the basis for the ruling, the defendant deprived the person being demolished of the right to choose the appraisal institution. Moreover, the appraisal result was not subject to cross-examination by both parties, the valuation of the house was inaccurate, and the content of the administrative ruling concerning the replacement of the demolished house was unclear and lacked enforceability. Furthermore, the demolished house had been leased to others before the demolition, and no agreement had been reached on the resettlement of the lessee. The plaintiff requested that the administrative ruling in question be annulled according to law.

Evidence submitted by the plaintiff:
1. A contract for contracted operation signed by Song Lili and Gao Hong and Yu Guijun, to prove that the plaintiff's house had been leased to others, and that when the house was demolished, the demolition party had made no arrangements for the lessee.
2. A videotape showing the condition of the house owned by Song Lili located at Xingfu Middle Road, Suqian, to prove the location of the house before demolition and the fact that it was leased to others.

Defendant's Defense: There was no impropriety in the procedure or result of Fangyuan Company's appraisal of the plaintiff's property. Our bureau's ruling based on Fangyuan Company's appraisal report was lawful. The plaintiff's claim that the administrative ruling was illegal on the ground that the demolition party Wanxing Company had not signed an agreement with the lessee of the demolished house lacks legal basis. The houses developed by the demolition party were under construction (forward delivery housing). At the time of our bureau's administrative ruling, the specific number, sequence numbers, orientations, etc. of the houses in that project could not be determined. It was not improper for the ruling not to address such content. We request that the ruling be upheld.

Evidence submitted by the defendant:
1. The reply (Su Ji Fa [2002] No. 72) from the Suqian Municipal Development Planning Commission approving the project proposal for the Zhongmao Department Store project of Suqian Zhongmao Department Store Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Department Store Company), to prove that the company's Zhongmao Department Store project had been lawfully approved and established.
2. The construction land planning permit (Su Gui Yong [2002] No. 107) and the red-line map from the Suqian Municipal Planning Bureau, the construction land approval document (Guo Tu Jian Zi No. 126 of 2002) from the Suqian Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, the house demolition permit (Chai Xu Zi [2003] No. 3), and the house demolition announcement, to prove that the Construction Bureau had lawfully obtained the construction land planning permit, construction land approval document, and house demolition permit, that the plaintiff's house fell within the designated demolition red-line area, and that a demolition announcement had been lawfully issued.
3. The business license of Fangyuan Company as a legal person, to prove that this entity is a qualified real estate appraisal consulting company with legal person status.
4. The qualification certificate of Fangyuan Company as a real estate price appraisal institution, to prove that this entity is a legally qualified real estate price appraisal institution.
5. A certificate from the Real Estate Industry Department of the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Construction, to verify that the appraisers Hu Zhongdong and Sun Quan are registered real estate appraisers.
6. The real estate appraisal report of Fangyuan Company, to prove that the Suqian Construction Bureau made its ruling based on the appraisal report of a statutory institution.
7. The title deed for Song Lili's house, to prove that the demolished house belonged to Song Lili.

Third Party's Defense: As the demolition party, all demolition activities carried out by our company were conducted in accordance with the law. The administrative ruling by the Suqian Construction Bureau on the demolition dispute was lawful and should be upheld.

Evidence submitted by the third party:
1. The reply from the Sucheng District People's Government of Suqian approving the compulsory demolition of the house of Song Lili, the person being demolished, to prove that the compulsory demolition was approved by the government department.
2. The minutes of the executive meeting of the head of the Sucheng District People's Government of Suqian, to prove that the leaders of the Sucheng District Government had formed a resolution on the demolition of the house.

After cross-examination at trial, it was determined that the evidence provided by the defendant, the Suqian Construction Bureau, could prove the lawfulness of the land use procedures for the demolition party and the qualification of the appraisal institution. However, the appraisal conclusion made by the appraisal institution commissioned unilaterally by the demolition party violated the provisions of Article 19 of the Jiangsu Province Urban Housing Demolition Management Regulations. The evidence provided by the Suqian Construction Bureau and the plaintiff, Song Lili, could prove that the owner of the demolished house was Song Lili, the person being demolished, and that the house was leased to others at the time of demolition. The evidence provided by the third party, Wanxing Company, could prove the lawfulness of its demolition actions.

The Sucheng District People's Court of Suqian found the following facts after trial:

On April 9, 2002, the Zhongmao Department Store construction project of the demolition party Wanxing Company was approved and established by the Suqian Municipal Development Planning Commission. On September 28, 2002, Wanxing Company obtained the construction land planning permit. On October 25, 2002, Wanxing Company obtained the state-owned land approval document. On March 24, 2003, Wanxing Company obtained the house demolition permit and acquired the qualification for demolition. On March 24, 2003, the Suqian Construction Bureau issued a demolition announcement, which specified the scope of demolition, the relocation deadline, and the demolition appraisal institution. The plaintiff, Song Lili's house, with a construction area of 637.07 square meters, located at Xingfu Middle Road, Suqian, fell within the demolition scope. Fangyuan Company, commissioned by Wanxing Company, appraised Song Lili's house slated for demolition. Because Song Lili objected to the compensation amount for the demolished house and demanded replacement in kind (产权调换), the parties failed to reach an agreement. On May 28, 2003, Wanxing Company applied to the Suqian Construction Bureau for a ruling on the demolition dispute. On June 5, 2003, the Suqian Construction Bureau, based on the appraisal price from Fangyuan Company, issued a ruling on the demolition dispute between Wanxing Company and Song Lili. Song Lili, dissatisfied with the ruling, initiated administrative litigation, requesting its annulment.

The Sucheng District People's Court of Suqian held:

Article 16 of the State Council Regulation on the Administration of Urban Housing Demolition stipulates: If the demolition party and the person being demolished, or the demolition party, the person being demolished, and the lessee of the house, fail to reach a demolition compensation and resettlement agreement, upon application by a party, the housing demolition management department shall make a ruling. Article 17 stipulates: If the person being demolished or the lessee of the house fails to relocate within the relocation period specified in the ruling, the people's government of the city or county where the house is located shall order the relevant department to carry out compulsory demolition, or the housing demolition management department shall lawfully apply to the people's court for compulsory demolition.

Article 19 of the Jiangsu Province Urban Housing Demolition Management Regulations stipulates: When conducting a price appraisal of a house to be demolished, the opinions of the person being demolished shall be solicited; if the demolition party and the person being demolished cannot reach an agreement, the housing demolition management department shall select the appraisal institution by lot from among qualified appraisal institutions, and the housing demolition management department shall announce the time and place of the lottery three days before the lottery at the demolition site.

In this case, the defendant, the Suqian Construction Bureau, upon the application of the third party, Wanxing Company, had the authority to make an administrative ruling on the demolition dispute between the plaintiff Song Lili and Wanxing Company in accordance with the provisions of the State Council Regulation on the Administration of Urban Housing Demolition. Although the State Council Regulation on the Administration of Urban Housing Demolition and the Jiangsu Province Urban Housing Demolition Management Regulations do not explicitly stipulate the procedures for administrative demolition rulings, administrative authorities must fully protect the legitimate rights of the parties when making a ruling and allow both parties to debate and make statements on the disputed issues. However, when the Suqian Construction Bureau made its ruling on the demolition dispute between Song Lili and Wanxing Company, it failed to allow Song Lili to make statements and defenses on the disputed issues, which was unfair. Its reliance solely on Wanxing Company's application and the appraisal result from an appraisal company commissioned unilaterally by Wanxing Company as the basis for the administrative ruling violated the provisions of the Jiangsu Province Urban Housing Demolition Management Regulations. Furthermore, although the ruling determined that Song Lili's house to be demolished would be compensated by means of replacement in kind (产权调换), it failed to clearly specify the specific location, floor, price, and other details of the house to be replaced for Song Lili, rendering the content of the demolition compensation ruling unenforceable. In conclusion, this administrative ruling violated legal provisions in its procedure and had content lacking enforceability; a new ruling should be made. Given that Song Lili's house has now been demolished, item (1) of the ruling content is upheld, and the remaining items are annulled.

Accordingly, on September 28, 2003, the Sucheng District People's Court of Suqian, in accordance with subparagraphs 1 and 3 of paragraph (2) of Article 54 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment:

1. Item (1) of the Su Jian Cai Zi [2003] No. 26 ruling of the Suqian Construction Bureau is upheld; items (2), (3), and (4) of the ruling are annulled;
2. The Suqian Construction Bureau shall make a new ruling on the housing demolition dispute between Song Lili and Wanxing Company in accordance with the law within 60 days from the effective date of this judgment.

After the judgment was announced, the Suqian Construction Bureau, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Suqian Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province. Song Lili indicated compliance with the first-instance court's judgment. Wanxing Company did not submit a written defense.

The Suqian Construction Bureau appealed, arguing: The administrative ruling made by our bureau in this case had a lawful procedure. Regarding the house to be replaced in kind, because the construction drawings for the building to be erected had not yet been drawn, it was impossible to determine the specific arrangement, orientation, and other details of the replacement house. We request that the judgment be amended according to law.

The Suqian Intermediate People's Court, after trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance. It further found that Song Lili clearly indicated that she had no objection to the moving expenses of RMB 6 per square meter and the resettlement fees of RMB 20 per square meter as determined in the Suqian Construction Bureau's ruling.

The Suqian Intermediate People's Court held:

The focus of the dispute in this case is: whether the appraisal report relied upon in the Suqian Construction Bureau's ruling was lawful and valid.

Wanxing Company's Zhongmao Department Store construction project was approved by the competent administrative department in accordance with statutory procedures, and Wanxing Company obtained the demolition permit for Song Lili's house on Xingfu Middle Road. When Wanxing Company was unable to reach a demolition agreement with the person being demolished, its application to the Suqian Construction Bureau for compulsory demolition of the house to be demolished was not improper. The Suqian Construction Bureau's decision in item (1) of the administrative ruling to set a deadline for the demolition of Song Lili's house, made in accordance with the provisions of the Regulation on the Administration of Urban Housing Demolition, complied with relevant administrative regulations and should be upheld by law. However, when the Suqian Construction Bureau ruled on the compensation amount for the demolished house, it relied solely on the appraisal conclusion of Fangyuan Company, which was commissioned unilaterally by Wanxing Company, violating the provisions of the Jiangsu Province Urban Housing Demolition Management Regulations. The appraisal of the demolished house in this case was conducted by Fangyuan Company on the unilateral commission of Wanxing Company, without the consent of Song Lili, the person being demolished. When Wanxing Company and Song Lili could not reach an agreement on the housing demolition matters, the Suqian Construction Bureau, in its administrative ruling, relied on the appraisal report of an appraisal company commissioned unilaterally by the demolition party, instead of selecting the appraisal institution by lot from among qualified appraisal institutions as required by regulations. This was an improper ruling on the housing demolition dispute between Wanxing Company and Song Lili and should be determined as lacking sufficient main evidence and violating procedure. Pursuant to subparagraph (2) of Article 62 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation, if the plaintiff or a third party presents evidence proving that the appraisal procedure of an expert conclusion adopted by the defendant in the administrative procedure is seriously illegal, the people's court shall not adopt it. Since the Suqian Construction Bureau failed to provide evidence to verify the lawfulness of the operational procedure for adopting the appraisal conclusion, item (2) of the Suqian Construction Bureau's ruling should be annulled according to law. As Song Lili did not object to the standards for demolition moving and resettlement compensation determined by the Suqian Construction Bureau in accordance with relevant regulations, these should be confirmed. Since the content of item (3) of the Suqian Construction Bureau's ruling lacked practical enforceability, the first-instance judgment's annulment of it was not improper. Given that Song Lili's house was leased to others at the time of demolition, when arranging transitional housing for Song Lili after the demolition of her house, the choices of Song Lili and the lessee should be respected. Although the Suqian Construction Bureau arranged transitional housing for Song Lili in its ruling, since Song Lili did not actually use it, the first-instance judgment's annulment of this content was also not improper.

In conclusion, on December 9, 2003, the Suqian Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with subparagraph (1) of Article 61 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
